channel.title: Internet & Cloud Health Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of major internet, cloud, AI and EDI VAN outages and cyber incidents. Published around noon Central, plus major incident alerts as they happen.

item.description: Northflank (cloud app hosting platform); Palo Alto Networks firewall customers (US, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, including US government-linked servers); AU Small Finance Bank (India), via a Salesforce-hosted platform; Chainalysis; About a dozen crypto project websites (flap.sh, Kintsu,…
item.content:encoded:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 31, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-10-31-0600.md (plus Scout's 2026-10-30-1800.md and 2026-10-31-0000.md runs for the rest of the window), with direct checks of the Oracle Cloud, Azure and EDI VAN status pages.

1. Cyber incidents

Northflank (cloud app hosting platform)

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Northflank says the activity may fit the wider attacks on AI credentials in Wiz's "Black October" report)
  • Date reported: Oct 30, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: After a Wiz threat alert, Northflank told every customer to assume their environment variables and stored secrets were decrypted and to rotate all of them, and users report their AI API keys were already misused. No root cause has been published yet, and the latest update (8:34 AM CDT Oct 31) added secret rotation for MySQL and Redis.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for any company or vendor that deploys apps on Northflank, since database passwords and API keys for outside services may be exposed and need revoking at the issuing provider.
  • Source: Northflank Status

Palo Alto Networks firewall customers (US, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, including US government-linked servers)

  • Industry: Technology providers / Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown (suspected China-nexus, AI-assisted)
  • Date reported: Oct 30, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Researchers at Dream and Palo Alto's Unit 42 say an attacker chained the PHP2Shell flaws with the Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to get root on about 25 internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls and management servers, then went after Active Directory and stole credentials. Palo Alto says about 0.02% of its firewalls were exposed and tells customers to lock management access to trusted IPs and patch.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. A rooted firewall gives an attacker a foothold into the whole network behind it, including connections to partners.
  • Source: Cybersecurity Dive

AU Small Finance Bank (India), via a Salesforce-hosted platform

  • Industry: Financial services
  • Threat actor: ScarlettGroup
  • Date reported: Oct 29–30, 2026
  • Status: Investigating (claimed by the group)
  • Summary: ScarlettGroup claims it took KYC records, ID numbers, credit reports, bank statements and loan files and is threatening to leak them. The bank says it's investigating a possible leak from a Salesforce-hosted platform that holds limited vehicle-loan customer data, and that its own banking systems are unaffected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. It's another case of data exposed through a SaaS vendor rather than the bank's own systems.
  • Source: ThePrint

Chainalysis

  • Industry: Technology providers (blockchain analytics)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 30–31, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Chainalysis says attackers used "offensive agentic techniques" to get into internal systems and tools, exposing customer names, email addresses, user IDs and organizational roles. It found no sign that passwords, tokens or investigation data were taken and warns customers to watch for phishing.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low to medium. Its customers include law enforcement and exchanges, so expect targeted phishing using the stolen contact list.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

About a dozen crypto project websites (flap.sh, Kintsu, pickle.finance, echelon.market and others)

  • Industry: Fintech / crypto
  • Threat actor: Unknown (sites redirected to Step Drainer phishing pages)
  • Date reported: Oct 30–31, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (ongoing)
  • Summary: Blockaid flagged 12 crypto project sites whose DNS was hijacked to send visitors to wallet-draining phishing pages. Users are told not to connect wallets and to revoke recent approvals.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for most businesses, though hijacking at the DNS level points to a shared registrar or DNS provider weakness worth watching.
  • Source: X news summary

2. AI service outages

  • Cursor's Automations, Cloud Agents, cursor.com and Grok Bot were degraded for about 44 minutes, from 1:04 to 1:47 AM CDT Oct 31. Status: resolved. Cursor Status

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • Akamai is investigating the remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-98432 on its platform and taking mitigation steps, with its last update at 9:08 PM CDT Oct 30 and no customer impact listed. Status: ongoing. OutageDB (Akamai advisory)
  • GPU cloud provider Lambda's lambda.ai was unreachable because of a DNS issue from 11:35 PM CDT Oct 30 to 2:07 AM CDT Oct 31. Status: resolved. Lambda Status
  • GitHub Actions, Pages deployments and webhooks were delayed from 12:50 to about 1:32 PM CDT Oct 30. Status: resolved. GitHub Status
  • Oracle Cloud (Normal Performance), Microsoft Azure (no active events), AWS, Google Cloud and Cloudflare had nothing major. Cleo, SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce are all operational, OpenText shows no new incidents (only a long-running Middle East regional outage from May), and I didn't get a direct read on the other EDI VAN providers.

4. Status changes

  • Twilio SMS and MMS delays to Altice (Optimum) subscribers in the US went from ongoing to resolved at about 5:15 PM CDT Oct 30. Twilio Status
  • PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) went from exploited in the wild to confirmed root compromises of about 25 Palo Alto firewalls when chained with Linux CVE-2026-46300 (details in section 1). Cybersecurity Dive

item.content:encoded:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 30, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-10-30-0600.md (plus Scout's 2026-10-30-0000.md run for the rest of the window), with direct checks of the Oracle Cloud, Azure and EDI VAN status pages.

1. Cyber incidents

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN customers (space, defense, policy research)

  • Industry: Technology providers / Government and defense
  • Threat actor: UAT-11473 (China-linked APT per Talos, with infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon's "Silent Train" network)
  • Date reported: Oct 28–29, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Cisco Talos says UAT-11473 exploited the max-severity SD-WAN authentication bypass CVE-2026-20127 (patched in February) to plant a custom malware framework called KeyDrift inside SD-WAN controllers. It hides in legitimate controller processes and steals the encryption keys that protect traffic between sites.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. SD-WAN controllers sit at the center of company and supplier networks, so anyone still unpatched should update, hunt for compromise and consider rotating keys.
  • Sources: Cisco Talos, BleepingComputer

Hugging Face model repositories (self-hosted AI servers)

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown (Pluto Security assesses a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking operator)
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed (ongoing)
  • Summary: Pluto Security found 31 fake Qwen2 model repositories with more than 32,000 downloads that run hidden Python when loaded with trust_remote_code, installing a cryptominer, persistence and in some versions a reverse shell. The campaign came back within days of a takedown, and a near-identical copy was still live when BleepingComputer reported it.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium to high for teams running self-hosted AI inference or CI jobs that pull models, since infected machines should be treated as compromised.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, Pluto Security

Trezor hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis (Southeast Asia)

  • Industry: Technology / retail (hardware supply chain)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 30, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Trezor says it received a credible report of an extra circuit board with a cellular module inside a Safe 5 bought from former reseller CryptoBilis, which reportedly reads the recovery phrase off the screen and sends it out. Trezor hasn't examined the device yet, no losses have been reported, and buyers from CryptoBilis since March 2026 are told to move funds to a new wallet.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for hardware bought through third-party resellers; it's the same distributor tied to the tampered Ledger devices.
  • Sources: Trezor, BleepingComputer

INTAX Inc. (Lexington, Kentucky)

  • Industry: Financial services (property-tax compliance)
  • Threat actor: Rhysida
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: Rhysida published what it says is 1.27 TB of data from INTAX, including client tax returns, bank details and IDs. The company hasn't confirmed it.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium to high for INTAX's corporate clients, whose tax and banking data could be in the leak.
  • Source: Quasar CyberTech

Archive of Our Own (AO3)

  • Industry: Technology / nonprofit
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: The AO3 fan-fiction site's outage is now described as a security incident, and its operator can't rule out theft of the user database (usernames, emails, IP addresses and hashed passwords). It expects two to four weeks of downtime and advises changing reused passwords.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for business, though leaked emails and password hashes feed credential-stuffing elsewhere.
  • Source: TechCrunch

Polymarket (via compromised DebugBear script)

  • Industry: Fintech / crypto
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Resolved
  • Summary: A compromised DebugBear monitoring script loaded on Polymarket's international site drained about $2.5 to $2.7 million from logged-in users. Polymarket halted trading for about an hour, removed the script and says it will reimburse users.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. It's a classic third-party script compromise, a reminder to audit what outside JavaScript runs on sensitive pages.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • Twilio SMS and MMS messages to Altice (Optimum) subscribers in the US have been delayed since about 7:10 PM CDT Oct 29, and Twilio has identified the cause but not fixed it yet. Status: ongoing. Twilio Status
  • AWS API Gateway HTTP APIs in US-West-2 (Oregon) had intermittent invoke errors and latency on and off from 9:27 AM to 6:15 PM CDT Oct 29, worst from 5:12 to 5:45 PM. Status: resolved. AWS Health
  • Infoblox Endpoint customers in North America had intermittent DNS resolution failures from about 10:57 AM to 2:23 PM CDT Oct 29. Status: resolved. OutageDB
  • Oracle Cloud (Normal Performance), Microsoft Azure (no active events), Google Cloud and Cloudflare had nothing major. Cleo, SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce and DiCentral are all operational, and I didn't get a direct read on the other EDI VAN providers.

4. Status changes

  • Binance hack went from investigating to confirmed: Binance links about $6.3 billion in stolen crypto to a compromised DevOps laptop, withdrawals are paused and expected to resume within about 48 hours. BleepingComputer
  • Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace went from ongoing to resolved: the package was pulled and the attacker's server is offline, but anyone who installed it between about 4:27 AM and 3:35 PM CDT Oct 29 still needs to remove the planted SSH key, run Cursor's cleanup scripts and rotate credentials. Cursor
  • Cisco ASA/FTD zero-day CVE-2026-76418 went from exploited and patched but not in CISA's list to added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, with a Nov 1 federal deadline. CISA
  • Palo Alto PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618) went from fixes still rolling out to fixed builds for every supported PAN-OS branch, with the last hotfix 11.1.7-h12 released Oct 29, while exploitation of exposed management interfaces continues. Palo Alto Networks
  • Amadeus airline reservation breach widened from Japan Airlines and JTA to also include ANA (about 37,800 customers), Cathay Pacific (about 53,000 bookings), Jin Air, Korean Air, Asiana and reportedly Condor, all tied to stolen Amadeus account credentials used from August 2023 to September 2026. Status: still ongoing, scope expanded. The Business Times

item.description: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS, CBP, ICE); Unnamed California city (police and 911 data); EWM Group (Peacocks, Bonmarché); Chrome Web Store search-hijacking campaign; Ledger hardware wallets sold in Singapore; Morrison Foerster; zkLink Nova bridge; Virtualine bulletproof hosting (law…
item.content:encoded:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 29, 2026 (past 24 hours) Source: Scout run 2026-10-29-0600.md (plus Scout's 2026-10-28-1800.md and 2026-10-29-0000.md runs for the rest of the window), with direct checks of the cloud, EDI VAN and Cloudflare status pages, CISA's exploited-vulnerability list and BleepingComputer.

1. Cyber incidents

U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS, CBP, ICE)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Hacktivists ("Icepick" leak, published by Distributed Denial of Secrets)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Distributed Denial of Secrets published names, phone numbers and assignments of about 40,000 DHS, CBP and ICE employees, reportedly pulled from a DHS Okta single sign-on directory. WIRED verified parts of the data, and Okta denies its own systems were compromised.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. If the data came from a misconfigured or abused identity directory, other agencies and contractors using the same setup could be exposed, and the leaked staff details invite targeted phishing.
  • Source: X news summary

Unnamed California city (police and 911 data)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Rhysida
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: Rhysida posted a leak-site listing claiming police and 911 data from a California city it didn't name. The claim hasn't been verified.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for business, but it's a public-safety system.
  • Source: RansomNews

EWM Group (Peacocks, Bonmarché)

  • Industry: Retail
  • Threat actor: Aurora
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: The Aurora group listed the UK fashion retailer EWM Group, which owns Peacocks and Bonmarché, on its leak site. Neither the scope nor the claim has been confirmed.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium for its suppliers and logistics partners if order or partner data was taken.
  • Source: RansomNews

Chrome Web Store search-hijacking campaign

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: Researchers found 319 Chrome extensions, with about 13.4 million combined installs, quietly sending users' searches through tracking servers to make advertising money from Bing and Yahoo.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium. Unvetted browser extensions on work PCs can see and redirect browsing traffic, so it's worth auditing what's installed.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

Ledger hardware wallets sold in Singapore

  • Industry: Technology / retail (hardware supply chain)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Singapore police say tampered Ledger hardware wallets sold through local retailers stole recovery phrases, costing two users about $2.7 million. Ledger has asked resellers in the region to stop sales while it reviews.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for hardware bought through third-party resellers, since the devices were compromised before they reached buyers.
  • Source: X news summary

Morrison Foerster

  • Industry: Legal services
  • Threat actor: SilentRansomGroup
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Claimed
  • Summary: SilentRansomGroup listed the US law firm Morrison Foerster on its leak site. The firm hasn't confirmed an incident.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Medium, because large law firms hold confidential deal and litigation files for many corporate clients.
  • Source: RansomNews

zkLink Nova bridge

  • Industry: Crypto / fintech
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 29, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: An attacker drained about $786,000 from the zkLink Nova Ethereum bridge late Oct 28 by reusing a valid message hash to forge withdrawals. zkLink paused the affected contracts and offered a 20% bounty.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low outside crypto.
  • Source: X news summary

Virtualine bulletproof hosting (law enforcement action)

  • Industry: Cybercrime infrastructure
  • Threat actor: Virtualine (hosting used by ransomware and other criminals)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Resolved (domain seized)
  • Summary: U.S. law enforcement seized the main domain of Virtualine, a hosting service advertised on crime forums for ransomware and other illegal activity.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Positive in the short term, though such groups usually move to new hosting quickly.
  • Source: BleepingComputer

2. AI service outages

  • Grok Bot, Cloud Agents and Origin were degraded from about 4:15 PM CDT Oct 28 for roughly two hours, leaving many bots unresponsive before service recovered. Status: resolved. X news summary

3. Internet, network, cloud and EDI VAN issues

  • A deep-sea fiber cut near Mtunzini, South Africa damaged the Seacom and EASSy submarine cables, slowing Safaricom home fiber and other Kenyan internet providers while traffic shifts to backup cables. Status: ongoing (repairs expected to take about a week). X news summary
  • Bet365 customers in several countries couldn't log in or saw missing bets for about two hours during Oct 28 evening football matches. Status: resolved. X news summary
  • AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure (no active events) and Oracle Cloud (Normal Performance) had no new incidents, and Cloudflare had only a few short, minor incidents that are all resolved. The EDI VAN pages I could read show nothing new: Cleo, SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce are all operational, and OpenText lists only an old Middle East item from May. I couldn't read the DiCentral, Descartes or ECGrid pages.

4. Status changes

  • FEC electronic filing went from investigating and offline to restored after an outage of nearly 41 hours; the FEC says voting wasn't affected and hasn't confirmed a data breach. X news summary
  • Cloudflare's Ashburn, Virginia network performance issue went from monitoring to resolved. Cloudflare Status

item.title: Internet & Cloud Health Digest — Oct 28, 2026
item.description: Federal Election Commission (FEC); Volt Typhoon "Silent Train" framework; GitHub "Gheist" token-theft campaign / Dodo Payments; Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767; Convertr (Brazilian e-commerce platform); Sony Network Communications (So-net / plala); Coinbase / Amplitude; Bithumb and Daishin…
item.content:encoded:
Daily internet & cloud health digest, Oct 28, 2026 (past 24 hours) Sources: Scout run 2026-10-28-1200.md (plus Scout's 1800, 0000 and 0600 runs) and direct checks of the EDI VAN, AI and CDN status pages.

1. Cyber incidents

Federal Election Commission (FEC)

  • Industry: Government
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: The FEC took its web-facing services offline, including electronic filing, after a "bad actor" tried to breach its systems around 9 PM CDT on Oct 26. The system was still offline Wednesday morning. Nobody has confirmed a successful intrusion or data theft, and voting isn't affected.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low for business, but campaign-finance filers can't submit their 24- and 48-hour reports a week before the midterms.
  • Sources: Politico, CNBC

Volt Typhoon "Silent Train" framework

  • Industry: Technology providers and critical infrastructure (network devices)
  • Threat actor: Volt Typhoon (China)
  • Date reported: Oct 28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Researchers found Volt Typhoon chaining hijacked routers, IoT devices and business network gear into short-lived relay paths. The paths are rebuilt daily and hide zero-day attacks. The exploited flaws include CVE-2026-16812, CVE-2026-20127 and a suspected zero-day in Quest KACE.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High, because edge and network devices at any company can be quietly used as relays for attacks.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, CyberScoop

GitHub "Gheist" token-theft campaign / Dodo Payments

  • Industry: Technology providers
  • Threat actor: Unknown ("Gheist" campaign)
  • Date reported: Oct 27–28, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Someone deleted a private Dodo Payments repository through the GitHub command-line tool, and the deletion left no trace in the audit log. Researchers tie it to a campaign using stolen tokens that has hit more than 850 GitHub accounts. GitHub is investigating.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High for software supply chains, since stolen developer tokens can be used to change or delete code.
  • Source: X news summary

Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767

  • Industry: Technology providers (an ERP system widely used in manufacturing and logistics)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Investigating
  • Summary: Attackers have started probing a critical flaw that Oracle patched on Oct 20. It lets an attacker who isn't logged in use SQL injection to run code on the server. Defused's decoy systems have caught attempts, but there are no confirmed compromises yet, and CISA hasn't added it to its list of exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High if attackers get it working, because EBS runs orders, finance and supply-chain work at many large companies. Patch now.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek

Convertr (Brazilian e-commerce platform)

  • Industry: Retail
  • Threat actor: A Magecart card-skimming group focused on Brazil
  • Date reported: Oct 26–27, 2026
  • Status: Resolved (skimmer removed, but how much damage it did is disputed)
  • Summary: Attackers planted a card skimmer in the Plausible analytics script that Convertr hosts itself and loads on every Convertr checkout. From Oct 24 to 27 it stole card details and taxpayer IDs. Convertr has removed it and says no real store checkouts were affected, but Sansec's findings dispute that.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: High. It's a textbook case of one shared third-party script hitting dozens of merchant checkouts at once.
  • Sources: BleepingComputer, Sansec

Sony Network Communications (So-net / plala)

  • Industry: Telecom / ISP
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
  • Summary: An Oct 19 intrusion at the Japanese internet providers So-net and plala exposed personal details of about 2.59 million current and former customers, along with about 54,000 email passwords. Sony shut the servers down on Oct 23 and has reset the affected passwords.
  • Supply chain / third-party risk: Low outside Japan's consumer customers, apart from the phishing risk.
  • Sources: So-net notice, Help Net Security

Coinbase / Amplitude

  • Industry: Financial services (through a third-party analytics vendor)
  • Threat actor: Unknown
  • Date reported: Oct 27–28, 2026
  • Status: Confirmed
